A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIG5-CHAT study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original generator evaluations, personality assessments, reasoning benchmark results, and trait-correlation analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds human evaluations, classifier-transfer experiments, prompting comparisons, and generated-dialogue evaluations.

M1.justification: The PSYCHSTEER logit-combination rule, five expert generators, five-word prefix, and downstream SFT/DPO approach remain. V2 explains how opposite trait levels form DPO preference pairs but does not establish a new core algorithm. Multi-trait steering is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds training and testing on the BigFive Essay dataset of 2,468 student essays, introducing an external long-form personality-classification domain. This differs from the 400-entry Big5PersonalityEssays resource discussed in both versions. Original dataset and benchmark coverage, including HumanEval and MBPP in the appendices, is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds GPT-4o-mini Post-Completion to the generator comparison, GPT-4o-mini prompting and three demonstration variants to personality assessments, and a generator without expert steering to the human dialogue comparison. Tables 7 and 11 establish their participation. V1's LLaMA-3-8B and GPT-4o-mini topic-based generator baselines remain in v2 Table 7.

E3.justification: V2 introduces blinded, randomized human comparisons with two annotators and 200 balanced examples per comparison, essay-only and combined classifier-training protocols, and resampled-demonstration evaluations. Main Table 3 changes from benchmark averaging to domain averaging. The preprocessing description replaces equidistant thresholds with quantile cutoffs; this establishes a reported setting revision without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test generation with and without expert steering, fixed versus resampled demonstrations, demonstration prompting on trained models, classifier transfer to essays, and personality expression in unseen SODA scenarios. Expanded lexical analyses and Appendix G's qualitative bias/hallucination cases substantially extend the original supplementary investigations.

E5.justification: V2 adds Cohen's kappa for human judgments, ranging from 0.41 to 0.61, and dispersion values for dataset statistics. Five-repeat personality-test standard deviations and reasoning standard errors are retained. No increase in repeated runs is established, and new significance assertions lack a specified statistical test.

E6.justification: V2 adds human-preference, prompting-variant, essay-transfer, and SODA-generation results. Reported high/low token averages change from 29.6/28.0 to 56.9/54.4, without establishing dataset regeneration. Generator extraversion accuracy changes from 80.1% to 80.0%. Reversed 70B aggregate assignments are corrected: DPO high/low averages become 47.0/52.3 instead of 52.3/47.0. Original Table 2 and individual reasoning scores remain unchanged; main Table 3's different summaries reflect domain averaging.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the formal range of gamma from [0,1] to [0,+infinity) and removes the incorrect assertion that gamma=1 fully adopts the expert's logits. Equation 1 remains unchanged. No substantial new theoretical development or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The dataset, training-based personality induction, human-like correlations, and reasoning contributions remain central. The conclusion narrows v1's statement that lower extraversion and neuroticism improve performance at all reasoning tasks to an association with better overall reasoning performance.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussions of single-trait steering, demographic representativeness, nonexpert human evaluators, and misuse. It interprets poor essay transfer and differences between DPO and SFT on generated dialogue. Appendix G connects personality extremes with unsupported catastrophic or hostile interpretations, extending v1's generic bias caveat with specific failure discussions.

D1.justification: V2 specifies DPO preference-pair construction, z-score preprocessing, tokenizers, demonstration sampling behavior, and the new Post-Completion prompt, and adds evaluation-framework links. Core hardware, training budgets, and the stated project code/data link remain. Some command-line and logging details from v1 Appendix B are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including Pennebaker and King, Hovy and Spruit, and Varadarajan et al. Section 4.2 and Table 6 extend dataset positioning, including the already-cited Machine Mindset, and argue against direct quantitative dataset comparisons. The existing related-work review is largely retained in Appendix C.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Background is condensed with its fuller discussion retained in Appendix B, Related Works moves to Appendix C, and intra-trait analysis moves to Appendix E.5. Implementation and reasoning appendices are reorganized, and multiple explanations and the conclusion are rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 switches to two-column layout, replaces the main benchmark table with domain summaries, expands dataset-statistics and comparison tables, and adds human-evaluation tables and classifier plots. Existing figures are retained with placement or caption changes; the crowd-comparison plots become vertically stacked.

improvement.justification: V1's realism claims relied largely on automated proxies and examples. V2's anonymized human comparisons, input-matched completion baseline, and generated-dialogue evaluations substantially strengthen their evidential basis. Corrected high/low averages and explicit failure and demographic discussions improve accuracy and transparency. Two nonexpert raters, weak essay transfer, and incompletely specified significance claims still limit the conclusions, but the new validation addresses an important weakness of v1.
